chunks: From him, from 'Abbas, from Rifa'ah, who said:
Ali عليه السلام used to say: If he performs eight circuits, then let him complete fourteen. I said: Should he perform four rak'ahs? He said: He performs two rak'ahs.

Thus, the correct way regarding these two reports is that we interpret them as applying to one who did that absentmindedly or forgetfully; for it is permissible for him to complete fourteen circuits. Repetition is only obligatory upon him when he did that deliberately. This is indicated by that.

key_terms.أَرْبَعَةَ عَشَرَ: fourteen, meaning the tawaf is completed as a doubled set of circuits
key_terms.الْإِعَادَةُ: repetition of the act due to invalidity or legal requirement
key_terms.ثَمَانِيَةً: eight circuits, indicating one extra round beyond the required number
key_terms.رَكْعَتَيْنِ: two rak'ahs of prayer performed after tawaf

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if someone performs eight circuits in tawaf instead of seven?
ai.summary: This report discusses the ruling for one who performs an extra circuit in tawaf, stating that if eight circuits were done unintentionally, the person may complete fourteen circuits and then perform two rak'ahs. The text further clarifies that repetition is only required when the extra circuit was done deliberately, making this a jurisprudential discussion of hajj ritual error and its legal consequence.
